faq.a: A light source is something that makes its own light, such as the Sun, other stars, fire, candles, light bulbs, torches and some animals like fireflies.

faq.q: Is the Moon a light source?
faq.a: No. The Moon makes no light of its own. It shines because sunlight bounces off it, which we call reflecting.
asks: Does the Moon make its own light?

faq.a: Sunlight hits the Moon's surface and some of it bounces off towards Earth. When that reflected light reaches our eyes, we see the Moon shining.

faq.q: Is a mirror a light source?
faq.a: No. A mirror only reflects light very well. In a completely dark room a mirror shows nothing at all.

faq.q: How does a firefly make light?
faq.a: A firefly mixes special chemicals in its tail that give off light without heat. It flashes to talk to other fireflies.

facts: The Moon reflects only about 12 percent of the sunlight that falls on it.
Fireflies make light by a chemical reaction called bioluminescence.
